chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Sariyy, from his uncle Ali ibn al-Sariyy, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The first of what was revealed upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was 'Bismillah ir-Rahman ir-Rahim, Iqra' bi-ismi Rabbik' and its last was 'Idha ja'a nasrullah'.

key_terms.إِذَا جَاءَ نَصْرُ اللَّهِ: When there comes the help of Allah
key_terms.بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ: In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful

ai.seo_question: What were the first and last verses revealed to Prophet Muhammad according to Shia sources?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the chronological bookends of the Quranic revelation, identifying the opening of Surah Al-Alaq as the first verse and the opening of Surah An-Nasr as the final revelation. In Shia scholarly tradition, this sequence underscores the transition from the initial command to recite and learn, to the ultimate divine victory and completion of the prophetic mission. It serves as a theological marker for the totality of the Quranic message received by the Prophet.
